subject: E-Commerce
title: Nearshoring After COVID
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Nearshoring After COVID.

hook.text: After COVID broke global supply chains, companies moved manufacturing closer to home.

buildup.text: COVID showed that depending on one country for manufacturing was risky. Lockdowns shut factories worldwide.

discovery.text: Nearshoring to Mexico or Central America cuts shipping time from 30 days to 3 days for the US market.

twist.text: Despite the nearshoring trend, China still dominates. It has infrastructure that takes decades to replicate.

climax.text: Supply chains are diversifying, not deglobalizing. The future is 'China plus one'—not China minus one.

punchline.text: 30 days from China, 3 from Mexico. Nearshoring is rewriting the supply chain.

quiz.question: What does 'China plus one' supply chain strategy mean?
options: Keeping China production but adding a second closer manufacturing source
